name: Hand fat freezing (cryolipolysis home kits)

card.summary: Consumer cooling devices and kits sold for freezing small fat pockets at home, aiming for a slimmer contour like in-clinic cryolipolysis.
card.aka: At-home CoolSculpting, DIY fat freezing, home cryolipolysis
card.note: Burn and frostbite injuries from home cold devices are documented in the medical literature.

quick.overview:
Home fat-freezing kits are consumer products, from handheld cooling devices and gel-pad wraps to improvised ice or dry-ice methods, offered as a way to reduce small fat pockets without a clinic visit. The goal is a slimmer waist, arm, thigh or chin contour.

The idea comes from professional cryolipolysis, introduced by Zeltiq Aesthetics under the CoolSculpting brand in 2010, which uses controlled cold on a fold of fat. Published studies of the professional procedure report modest fat-thickness reductions, while research on home devices is limited to case reports of injuries.
quick.how: Users apply a cooling device or pad to a targeted area for a set time, usually repeating sessions, and combine it with diet and exercise. Clinicians who comment on these products note that home devices do not reproduce the controlled temperature and cooling rate of in-office machines.
quick.risks: Reported harms include frostbite, blistering, full-thickness burns and scarring, particularly when temperatures are colder than intended or protective barriers are skipped. Dermatology sources also name paradoxical fat enlargement as a rare effect of professional cryolipolysis.

lead: Home fat-freezing kits are consumer versions of cryolipolysis, a procedure that uses cold to reduce subcutaneous fat in a targeted area. The professional technology was introduced in the United States in 2010 by Zeltiq Aesthetics as CoolSculpting, and Allergan acquired it in 2017 [1]. Home-use products and improvised methods aim to give a similar contour change, for example a slimmer abdomen, flank or arm, without a clinic visit.

Systematic reviews of the professional procedure report modest fat reductions, with ultrasound fat thickness down by about 2.0 to 5.1 mm in a 2023 review that rated data quality low [1]. For home devices, the published literature consists mainly of case reports of thermal injuries [2].

angle.text: People use these kits to try to shrink a local fat pocket for a leaner contour. Professional cryolipolysis shows modest measured reductions; no published trial has measured results from home devices.

infobox: Professional systems FDA-cleared for specific areas [1]

paras: Cryolipolysis places a fold of fat between cooling panels so that cold damages fat cells while sparing overlying skin [3]. Home kits range from commercial devices bought online to improvised methods such as ice packs or dry ice, which a published case series links to burns [2].

Reviews of professional treatment report skinfold reductions and high patient satisfaction, with the 2023 review concluding that it is safe and modestly effective on low-quality data [1]. Healthline notes that many supporting studies were funded by companies with a financial interest [3]. No controlled studies of consumer devices were located.

A published case report describes a woman who used an online-purchased machine at colder temperatures than recommended and without the protective membrane, developing blistering and mixed-depth burns over 2% of body surface area and a hypertrophic scar [2]. The authors cite other cases, including burns after dry ice use following a video and burns from salon treatments, and call for stricter regulation of devices and retailers [2].

Common effects of professional treatment are redness, numbness, swelling and bruising, and paradoxical adipose hyperplasia occurs in roughly 0.12 to 1.0 percent of cases [1]. People with cryoglobulinemia, cold agglutinin disease or paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria are advised not to have it [3].
No studies found on home-use devices. Related research on professional cryolipolysis includes systematic reviews of 18 to 19 studies showing modest fat reductions [1].

timeline.event: Zeltiq Aesthetics introduces CoolSculpting in the US [1].
